prevention: Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to birds and sunlight
cultural: Intercrop groundnut with sunflower or castor as trap crop (1:10 ratio)
mechanical: Handpick egg masses and gregarious young larvae; destroy them in kerosene water
physical: Use light traps @ 1 trap/ha to collect and destroy adult moths
biological: Spray Spodoptera NPV @ 250 LE/ha or release Trichogramma chilonis @ 50 000/ha
chemical: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2 mL/L or Novaluron 10% EC @ 1 mL/L if ETL crossed
threshold: 1 egg mass or 1-2 larvae per meter row
notes: Prioritize trap cropping and egg mass collection before chemical intervention

monitoring: Monitor light traps and inspect 20 plants/field for mines
prevention: Crop rotation with non-host crops like cereal/millets
cultural: Maintain optimum crop density (30cm x 10cm); avoid drought stress
mechanical: Handpick and destroy mined leaflets in early stages
physical: Use light traps to attract adult moths during night hours
threshold: 1 mine per leaflet or 5-10% leaflet damage
notes: Do not spray chemical insecticides if natural parasitoid activity is high

monitoring: Inspect 10 young terminal shoots per acre for silvering
prevention: Maintain weed-free field bunds; destroy alternate host weeds
cultural: Maintain field moisture through timely irrigation to suppress thrips
mechanical: Use blue sticky traps @ 25 traps/ha for monitoring and mass trapping
physical: Erect blue sticky traps at canopy level
biological: Conserve natural predators like predatory thrips and anthocorid bugs
notes: Thrips vector Peanut Bud Necrosis Virus; early management is vital

monitoring: Inspect lower leaves starting 30 days after sowing
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds; adopt resistant/tolerant varieties (GPBD-4, G2-52)
cultural: Remove crop debris after harvest; maintain recommended spacing (30cm x 10cm)
mechanical: Remove heavily infected lower leaves in early stage
physical: Avoid sprinkler irrigation during evening hours
biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg seed
chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.5 mL/L
notes: Combine cultural management with timely fungicide application

monitoring: Monitor crop canopy from 45 DAS onwards
prevention: Adopt crop rotation with sorghum or maize for 2 seasons
cultural: Avoid dense canopy planting; ensure adequate air circulation
mechanical: Destroy volunteer groundnut plants and infected haulms
physical: Solarize soil during hot summer months
biological: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L foliar spray
threshold: 5% leaf area affected on lower canopy
notes: Hexaconazole controls both Late Leaf Spot and Rust simultaneously

prevention: Use resistant/tolerant rice varieties; clip leaf tips before transplanting
cultural: Optimum field drainage; avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizers
mechanical: Handpick egg masses from seedling leaves; destroy egg masses
physical: Use light traps to collect adult moths
biological: Release Trichogramma japonicum @ 100 000/ha at 7-day intervals (4 releases)
chemical: Broadcast Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 10 kg/ha in 2-3 cm standing water
threshold: 2 egg masses/m2 or 5% dead hearts or 2% white ears
notes: Clipping leaf tips before transplanting destroys egg masses laid near leaf tips

monitoring: Monitor lower stem base of 20 hills randomly
prevention: Adopt wide row planting (20cm x 15cm) with alleyways every 2 meters
cultural: Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation; split nitrogen application
mechanical: Pass rope over canopy to dislodge planthoppers into water
physical: Use light traps for population monitoring
biological: Conserve natural enemies: spiders, mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus), and damselflies
chemical: Spray Pymetrozine 50% WDG @ 0.6 g/L or Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 0.4 g/L
threshold: 5-10 planthoppers per hill during vegetative stage
notes: Drain standing water immediately upon BPH buildup to break pest multiplication

monitoring: Inspect nursery and main field leaves weekly
prevention: Use certified seed of blast-resistant varieties (Rasi, KMP-101, TNS-27)
cultural: Avoid excess nitrogen application; apply N in 3 split doses with K
mechanical: Remove collateral weed hosts from field bunds
physical: Avoid evening irrigation that leaves leaves wet overnight
biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed
chemical: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 mL/L
threshold: 1% leaf area covered with spindle spots or neck blast initiation
notes: Tricyclazole is the primary recommendation for neck blast prevention

monitoring: Install FAW pheromone traps @ 12 traps/ha from germination
prevention: Deep summer ploughing; intercrop maize with cowpea or pigeonpea (4:2)
cultural: Clean cultivation; apply sand/soil + neem cake in whorls at 15-20 DAS
mechanical: Crush egg masses and young larvae in whorl manually
physical: Use light traps to catch adult moths
biological: Whorl application of Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5 g/L or Nomuraea rileyi @ 3 g/L
chemical: Whorl spray of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 mL/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5 mL/L
threshold: 5% whorl damage (seedling stage) to 10% whorl damage (mid-stage)
notes: Direct nozzle straight down into central whorl for effective larval contact

prevention: Use resistant hybrids; practice crop rotation with pulses or oilseeds
cultural: Destroy crop residues post-harvest; maintain balanced NPK nutrition
mechanical: Remove and burn lower infected leaves at early stage
physical: Ensure proper field drainage and air ventilation
biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg seed
chemical: Foliar spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole @ 1 mL/L
threshold: 1-2 long elliptical lesions per leaf on 10% plants
notes: Early removal of infected lower leaves slows upper canopy disease spread

monitoring: Monitor nut drop under canopy prior to and during monsoon
prevention: Provide effective field drainage; remove infected fallen nuts
cultural: Sanitize palm crowns before monsoon; clear dried inflorescence debris
mechanical: Fit polythene covers/caps over nut bunches prior to monsoon rain
physical: Collect and destroy fallen infected nuts by burning or deep burial
biological: Place Trichoderma harzianum coir-pith bio-blocks in crown leaf axils
chemical: Spray 1% Bordeaux Mixture or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L with sticker
threshold: First nut drop or prophylactic pre-monsoon timing
notes: Prophylactic Bordeaux mixture spray before monsoon is essential in high rainfall zones

monitoring: Inspect palm crown for yellowing of spear leaf
prevention: Maintain clean palm crowns; avoid waterlogging around trunk base
cultural: Remove infected tissue from top of crown down to healthy tissue
mechanical: Cut and burn severely rot-damaged palms to prevent garden spread
physical: Protect top crown from rain penetration
biological: Apply Trichoderma paste to crown after tissue cleaning
chemical: Apply 10% Bordeaux Paste on cleaned crown bud
threshold: At initial yellowing or wilting of top spear leaf
notes: Early detection and crown cleaning save the palm from total loss

monitoring: Inspect trunk bases for reddish-brown exudate bleeding
prevention: Isolate affected palm by digging 30cm wide x 60cm deep trench around base
cultural: Apply organic manure + neem cake @ 2 kg/palm annually
mechanical: Remove bracket fungi (fruiting bodies) from trunk base and burn
biological: Soil drenching with Trichoderma viride @ 25 g/palm in FYM
chemical: Base drenching with Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2 mL/L (5-10 L/palm)
threshold: First sign of stem bleeding or bracket fungus emergence
notes: Trench isolation prevents root-to-root transmission to adjacent healthy palms
